extra_vocab.en: a person who makes a phone call
extra_vocab.note: 多益電話情境最常見的字，常出現在祕書、客服或櫃檯的對話裡，例如轉接電話、請來電者留言。

example.en: We receive about fifty callers every day at the help desk.
example.zh: 客服台每天大約接到五十通來電。

example.en: The caller ID showed that the call came from Tokyo.
example.zh: 來電顯示顯示這通電話來自東京。

example.en: Please do not give company information to an unknown caller.
example.zh: 請不要把公司資訊告訴不明來電者。

example.en: Mr. Lee is a regular caller to our service center.
example.zh: 李先生是我們服務中心的常客來電者。

examples.en: The caller asked to speak with the sales manager.
examples.zh: 來電者想和業務經理通話。

examples.en: Our system shows the caller's name on the screen.
examples.zh: 我們的系統會在螢幕上顯示來電者的名字。

examples.en: A caller left a message for you this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上有人打電話來留言給你。

confusable.diff: 發音接近，但 collar 是「衣領」，和電話無關。

example.en: Employees should wear shirts with a collar on client visits.
example.zh: 員工拜訪客戶時應穿有領子的襯衫。

similar.diff: caller 是打電話的人；visitor 是親自到場拜訪的人。

example.en: A visitor is waiting for you at the front desk.
example.zh: 有一位訪客在櫃檯等你。

example.en: The operator connected the caller to the sales office.
example.zh: 總機把來電轉給業務辦公室。

example.en: The receptionist answers all calls before nine o'clock.
example.zh: 櫃檯人員在九點前接聽所有電話。

example.en: Every customer can call our help line for free.
example.zh: 每位顧客都可以免費撥打我們的客服專線。

extra_vocab.zh: 休閒的、非正式的、隨意的
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於服裝規定（casual dress）、非正式會議與語氣。要看情境判斷是「休閒」還是「隨便、不用心」，後者語氣偏負面。

example.en: She casually mentioned the price change during the meeting.
example.zh: 她在會議中不經意地提到價格變動。

example.en: Casual dress is fine for the company picnic this weekend.
example.zh: 這個週末的公司野餐可以穿休閒服裝。

example.en: We had a casual conversation with the client before the meeting.
example.zh: 會議前我們和客戶輕鬆聊了一下。

example.en: Many offices have a casual Friday once a week.
example.zh: 許多公司每週有一天週五便服日。

examples.en: Our office allows employees to wear casual clothes on Fridays.
examples.zh: 我們公司允許員工星期五穿便服。

examples.en: We had a casual talk about the project after lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐後我們輕鬆聊了一下這個專案。

examples.en: Please keep the tone of this email casual but polite.
examples.zh: 這封電子郵件的語氣請輕鬆但有禮貌。

examples.en: The interview was casual, so I felt relaxed.
examples.zh: 這場面試很輕鬆，所以我不緊張。

confusable.diff: 拼法接近，但 causal 是「因果的」，和輕鬆、隨意無關。

example.en: The study found a causal link between training and sales.
example.zh: 這份研究發現訓練與銷售之間有因果關係。

similar.diff: informal 強調「不正式」；casual 還帶有輕鬆、不拘束的感覺。

example.en: We had an informal chat before the formal presentation.
example.zh: 正式簡報前，我們先做了非正式的交談。

similar.diff: relaxed 形容氣氛或人放鬆；casual 多形容服裝、態度或場合。

example.en: The relaxed atmosphere helped everyone share new ideas.
example.zh: 輕鬆的氣氛讓大家更願意分享新點子。

example.en: A formal dress code is required for the awards dinner.
example.zh: 頒獎晚宴要求穿正式服裝。

example.en: Please wear comfortable shoes for the factory tour.
example.zh: 參觀工廠請穿舒適的鞋子。

senses.en: relaxed and not formal in style
senses.distinguish: 後面常接 clothes、dress、jacket 等和穿著有關的字。

example.en: He wore a casual jacket to the team lunch.
example.zh: 他穿了一件休閒外套去參加團隊午餐。

senses.distinguish: 後面常接 meeting、talk、conversation，指場合不正式。

example.en: This is only a casual meeting, so you needn't prepare.
example.zh: 這只是個非正式會議，你不必準備。

senses.en: done without much thought or care

example.en: His casual attitude toward deadlines made the manager worried.
example.zh: 他對截止日期的隨便態度讓經理很擔心。

extra_vocab.en: the person who leads a meeting or a group
extra_vocab.note: 多益會議與公司組織的常見字，用來指主持會議或領導委員會的人，不分男女。常和 board、committee、meeting 一起出現。

example.en: Both chairpersons agreed to share the meeting schedule.
example.zh: 兩位主席同意共享會議時程。

example.en: The board decided to appoint a new chairperson in May.
example.zh: 董事會決定在五月任命新的主席。

example.en: Members will elect a chairperson by a simple vote.
example.zh: 成員將以簡單投票選出主席。

example.en: She is the chairperson of the planning committee.
example.zh: 她是企劃委員會的主席。

example.en: The deputy chairperson will lead the meeting today.
example.zh: 今天由副主席主持會議。

examples.en: The chairperson opened the meeting at nine o'clock.
examples.zh: 主席在九點整宣布開會。

examples.en: We will choose a new chairperson at the annual meeting.
examples.zh: 我們將在年度會議上選出新的主席。

examples.en: The chairperson of the board will visit our branch next week.
examples.zh: 董事會主席下週會來我們分公司。

confusable.diff: chair 是「椅子」，也可當「主席」的簡短說法。
confusable.usage: chair 也可當動詞，chair a meeting 是「主持會議」；chairperson 只當名詞。

example.en: Ms. Wang will chair the meeting this afternoon.
example.zh: 王小姐今天下午將主持會議。

similar.diff: moderator 多用於座談、討論會，負責控制發言；chairperson 是會議或組織的負責人。

example.en: The moderator asked each speaker to keep to five minutes.
example.zh: 主持人請每位講者控制在五分鐘內。

example.en: The president will speak to all staff on Monday.
example.zh: 總裁星期一會對全體員工說話。

example.en: The director approved the new budget this morning.
example.zh: 主管今天早上核准了新預算。

derived.link: chairperson = chair + person，坐在主位的人；chair 本身就能當「主席」
chair + man，像 salesman、businessman，現在多改用 chairperson
chair + woman，和 chairman 相對，指女性主席

extra_vocab.en: to shout happily to show support, or to make someone feel happier
extra_vocab.note: 多益常出現在公司活動、慶祝成果的場合。cheer for 是「為…加油」，cheer up 是「使打起精神」，Cheers! 則是乾杯或道謝的口語說法。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: cheer up 當「使振奮」時可以拆開，代名詞要放中間：cheer him up，不能說 cheer up him。

example.en: The whole team cheers when we win a big contract.
example.zh: 每次我們拿下大合約，全隊都會歡呼。

example.en: Cheers filled the hall after the award speech.
example.zh: 頒獎致詞結束後，大廳充滿歡呼聲。

example.en: Everyone cheered when the manager announced the bonus.
example.zh: 經理宣布獎金時，大家都歡呼起來。

example.en: Staff members were cheering for the winning team.
example.zh: 員工們正在為獲勝的隊伍歡呼。

example.en: A small gift can cheer up a tired coworker.
example.zh: 一份小禮物能讓疲累的同事打起精神。

example.en: We all cheered for our team at the company sports day.
example.zh: 公司運動會上，我們都為自己的隊伍加油。

example.en: Many employees came to cheer on the runners at the charity race.
example.zh: 許多員工來慈善路跑為跑者加油。

example.en: The staff gave a cheer when sales passed the target.
example.zh: 業績超過目標時，員工歡呼了一聲。

examples.en: The audience cheered when the CEO finished the speech.
examples.zh: 執行長演講結束時，觀眾歡呼起來。

examples.en: Your kind email really cheered me up this morning.
examples.zh: 你親切的電子郵件讓我今天早上心情變好了。

examples.en: Cheers, everyone! Let's celebrate the new partnership with a toast.
examples.zh: 大家乾杯！讓我們一起慶祝新的合作關係。

confusable.diff: 發音和拼法接近：cheer 是「歡呼」，chair 是「椅子」。

example.en: Please bring a chair to the meeting room.
example.zh: 請搬一張椅子到會議室。

similar.diff: applaud 是拍手稱讚，語氣較正式；cheer 是大聲歡呼加油。

example.en: The audience applauded after the manager's short speech.
example.zh: 經理簡短致詞後，觀眾鼓掌。

similar.diff: encourage 是用話語或行動鼓勵人；cheer on 偏向現場加油。

example.en: My manager encouraged me to join the training program.
example.zh: 我的經理鼓勵我參加訓練課程。

example.en: We encourage staff to share their ideas at meetings.
example.zh: 我們鼓勵員工在會議上分享想法。

example.en: Everyone applauded the team for finishing early.
example.zh: 大家為團隊提早完成而鼓掌。

example.en: We will celebrate our tenth anniversary next month.
example.zh: 我們下個月將慶祝十週年。

example.en: The crowd cheered as the new store opened its doors.
example.zh: 新店開門時，群眾歡呼起來。

example.en: A loud cheer came from the sales department.
example.zh: 業務部傳來一陣大聲的歡呼。

senses.en: to shout to show support or joy

example.en: Fans cheered loudly as the runners crossed the finish line.
example.zh: 跑者衝過終點線時，球迷大聲歡呼。

senses.distinguish: 後面接 up，或主詞是會讓人心情變好的事物時，就是「使振奮」。

example.en: A short phone call can cheer up a worried client.
example.zh: 一通簡短的電話能讓擔心的客戶安心一些。

extra_vocab.note: 多益常用來形容天氣或辦公室冷氣太冷，也可以形容氣氛或態度冷淡，例如 a chilly reception。比 cold 的冷度輕一些。

example.en: The office feels chillier than it did yesterday.
example.zh: 辦公室今天感覺比昨天更冷。

example.en: Tomorrow will be the chilliest day of the week.
example.zh: 明天將是這週最冷的一天。

example.en: Chilly weather may delay the outdoor event this weekend.
example.zh: 涼冷的天氣可能會延後這個週末的戶外活動。

example.en: Our offer received a chilly reception from the client.
example.zh: 客戶對我們的提案反應冷淡。

example.en: I feel chilly, so could you turn off the fan?
example.zh: 我覺得冷，可以請你關掉電風扇嗎？

example.en: A chilly wind made the outdoor interview uncomfortable.
example.zh: 冷風讓這場戶外訪談很不舒服。

examples.en: It was chilly in the morning, so I brought a jacket.
examples.zh: 早上天氣涼，所以我帶了外套。

examples.en: The meeting room is a little chilly because of the air conditioner.
examples.zh: 因為冷氣的關係，會議室有點冷。

examples.en: Evenings can be chilly in Seattle, so pack a coat.
examples.zh: 西雅圖的晚上可能很涼，記得帶外套。

examples.en: The new plan got a chilly reception from the staff.
examples.zh: 新計畫得到員工冷淡的反應。

confusable.diff: 發音相同，拼法只差一個 l；chili 是「辣椒」。

example.en: The restaurant serves a chili sauce with every dish.
example.zh: 這家餐廳每道菜都附辣椒醬。

similar.diff: cool 是涼爽、舒服；chilly 有點冷、不太舒服。

example.en: The weather is cool and nice for a walk after work.
example.zh: 天氣涼爽，很適合下班後散步。

similar.diff: cold 比 chilly 更冷，是一般的「冷」。

example.en: The cold weather forced us to close the office early.
example.zh: 寒冷的天氣迫使我們提早關閉辦公室。

example.en: Please keep the storage room cool and dry.
example.zh: 請讓倉庫保持涼爽乾燥。

example.en: The cold drinks are in the refrigerator.
example.zh: 冷飲放在冰箱裡。

example.en: The hotel gave us a warm welcome at the door.
example.zh: 飯店在門口熱情歡迎我們。

derived.link: chill 是「冷意」，chilly = chill + -y，有一點冷的，像 windy、sunny

senses.distinguish: 形容天氣、房間、風時，就是「有點冷」。

example.en: The hall was chilly before the heater was turned on.
example.zh: 暖氣開啟前，大廳很冷。

senses.distinguish: 形容反應、氣氛、態度（reception、mood）時，指「不友善」。

example.en: The chilly mood in the room ended the talks.
example.zh: 房間裡冷淡的氣氛讓談判結束了。

extra_vocab.en: a person who works in a shop, hotel, or office and does simple jobs
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於購物、飯店、銀行與辦公室情境。常和工作場所連在一起，如 sales clerk、hotel clerk、office clerk，指一般職員而不是主管。

example.en: Two clerks are working at the front desk today.
example.zh: 今天有兩位職員在櫃檯值班。

example.en: A sales clerk showed the customer how to use the machine.
example.zh: 一位銷售店員向顧客示範如何使用這台機器。

example.en: We are hiring an office clerk for the accounting team.
example.zh: 我們正在為會計組徵求一位辦公室事務員。

example.en: The front desk clerk checked our reservation on the computer.
example.zh: 櫃檯人員用電腦查了我們的訂房。

example.en: The shipping clerk will send the boxes tomorrow morning.
example.zh: 出貨人員明天早上會寄出這些箱子。

examples.en: The clerk helped me find a larger size.
examples.zh: 店員幫我找到了大一點的尺寸。

examples.en: The hotel clerk gave us two room keys.
examples.zh: 飯店櫃檯人員給了我們兩把房間鑰匙。

examples.en: She works as a clerk in the accounting department.
examples.zh: 她在會計部門擔任事務員。

examples.en: Please give the form to the bank clerk.
examples.zh: 請把這份表格交給銀行行員。

confusable.diff: 拼法和發音有點接近，但 clock 是「時鐘」。

example.en: The clerk checked the clock and closed the store.
example.zh: 店員看了一下時鐘，就關了店門。

similar.diff: assistant 是協助主管或同事的人，範圍比 clerk 廣；clerk 偏向處理文書或櫃檯工作。

example.en: My assistant will send you the schedule today.
example.zh: 我的助理今天會把時程表寄給你。

similar.diff: salesperson 專指賣東西的人；clerk 也可以是飯店或辦公室的職員。

example.en: The salesperson explained the discount to the customer.
example.zh: 銷售人員向顧客說明折扣。

example.en: The cashier gave me a receipt and my change.
example.zh: 收銀員給了我收據和零錢。

example.en: Our assistant books all the meeting rooms for us.
example.zh: 我們的助理幫我們預訂所有會議室。

example.en: The receptionist asked the visitor to sign in.
example.zh: 接待人員請訪客簽到。

derived.link: clerk 的形容詞，指文書、辦公室的工作，如 clerical work、clerical staff

senses.en: a person who serves customers in a shop or hotel
senses.distinguish: 和 shop、hotel、store 一起出現時，指服務客人的人。

example.en: The clerk at the shop wrapped the gift for me.
example.zh: 店裡的店員幫我包好了禮物。

senses.en: a person who does office work such as filing and keeping records
senses.distinguish: 和 office、accounting、records 一起出現時，指做文書工作的人。

example.en: The clerk updates the customer records in the system every afternoon.
example.zh: 這位事務員每天下午更新系統裡的客戶資料。

extra_vocab.en: the number of copies sold, or the movement of things from person to person
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於報章雜誌的發行量（newspaper circulation）、錢或物品的流通（in circulation），以及血液循環。要看前後文判斷是哪一種意思。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 表示發行量時常寫成 a circulation of 50,000；in circulation 前面不加冠詞。

example.en: Newspaper circulation has dropped in the last five years.
example.zh: 報紙發行量在過去五年下滑。

example.en: Only a few copies of the old brochure are still in circulation.
example.zh: 舊的宣傳冊只剩少數幾本還在流通。

example.en: Please call the circulation department to change your address.
example.zh: 要更改地址，請打電話給發行部門。

example.en: Cold offices can be hard for people with poor circulation.
example.zh: 太冷的辦公室對血液循環不好的人很難受。

examples.en: The newspaper has a circulation of over fifty thousand.
examples.zh: 這份報紙的發行量超過五萬份。

examples.en: The new coin will be put into circulation next month.
examples.zh: 新硬幣將在下個月開始流通。

examples.en: A draft of the plan is already in circulation in the office.
examples.zh: 這份計畫的草稿已經在辦公室裡傳閱。

examples.en: Regular walks at lunch can improve your blood circulation.
examples.zh: 午餐時規律散步能改善血液循環。

similar.diff: distribution 偏指貨物或資料的分送；circulation 偏指報刊的發行量或流通。

example.en: The distribution of the new product starts next week.
example.zh: 新產品的配送下週開始。

similar.diff: readership 是「讀者群」；circulation 是「發行份數」。

example.en: Our readership grew after we added an online edition.
example.zh: 我們推出線上版後，讀者群增加了。

example.en: We changed our distribution method to save shipping costs.
example.zh: 我們改變配銷方式以節省運費。

example.en: Please renew your magazine subscription before the end of June.
example.zh: 請在六月底前續訂你的雜誌。

derived.link: circle（圓）+ -ate，繞圈流動；circulate + -ion 變名詞，像 educate → education
circle + -ar，像圓一樣的；n. 指在大家之間「轉圈」傳閱的通知單

senses.en: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold
senses.distinguish: 和 newspaper、magazine、readers 一起出現時，指賣出的份數。

example.en: The magazine's circulation grew after the new design.
example.zh: 雜誌改版後，發行量增加了。

senses.en: the movement of money, goods, or information among people
senses.distinguish: 和 money、coin、information 一起出現，或搭配 in circulation 時，指流通。

example.en: The circulation of fake news can hurt a brand.
example.zh: 假消息的散播會傷害品牌。

senses.en: the movement of blood around the body
senses.distinguish: 和 blood、body、health 一起出現時，指身體的循環。

example.en: Good circulation helps workers stay warm in cold offices.
example.zh: 良好的血液循環能幫助員工在冷的辦公室保暖。

extra_vocab.zh: 慢性的、長期的、積習難改的
extra_vocab.en: lasting for a long time and hard to fix
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於醫療、保險與職場報導，指長期存在又難以根除的疾病或問題，如 chronic illness、chronic shortage。語氣通常偏負面。

example.en: Employees with a chronic illness may ask for flexible hours.
example.zh: 有慢性病的員工可以申請彈性工時。

example.en: Hospitals face a chronic shortage of nurses in many cities.
example.zh: 許多城市的醫院長期缺少護理師。

example.en: Late delivery is a chronic problem for this supplier.
example.zh: 延遲交貨是這家供應商的長期問題。

example.en: She sees a doctor regularly for her chronic pain.
example.zh: 她因為慢性疼痛而定期看醫生。

examples.en: Chronic back pain can make it hard to work long hours.
examples.zh: 慢性背痛可能讓人很難長時間工作。

examples.en: Chronic lateness may affect your performance review this year.
examples.zh: 長期遲到可能影響你今年的績效考核。

examples.en: The company has a chronic shortage of skilled workers.
examples.zh: 這家公司長期缺乏有技術的員工。

examples.en: This insurance plan covers care for chronic illness.
examples.zh: 這個保險方案涵蓋慢性病的照護。

similar.diff: long-term 是中性的「長期的」；chronic 常帶負面，指長期存在的疾病或問題。

example.en: We need a long-term plan to solve the cost problem.
example.zh: 我們需要一個長期計畫來解決成本問題。

similar.diff: persistent 強調「持續不斷」；chronic 強調「長期且難以根治」。

example.en: Persistent noise from the street disturbs our office.
example.zh: 街上持續不斷的噪音干擾我們辦公室。

example.en: The delay caused a serious problem for our clients.
example.zh: 這次延誤給我們的客戶帶來嚴重問題。

example.en: Constant changes make it hard to finish the project.
example.zh: 不斷的變更讓專案很難完成。

example.en: We have an ongoing problem with the printer.
example.zh: 我們的印表機一直有問題。

derived.link: chronic + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quickly；常說 chronically late（老是遲到）

senses.en: lasting a long time, used for illnesses
senses.distinguish: 和 illness、disease、condition、pain 一起出現時，指慢性病痛。

example.en: He takes medicine every day for a chronic condition.
example.zh: 他因為慢性病每天服藥。

senses.en: happening again and again for a long time
senses.distinguish: 和 problem、shortage、delay 一起出現時，指長期存在的問題。

example.en: Chronic delays in shipping have upset many customers.
example.zh: 運送的長期延誤讓許多客戶不滿。
